source.author: Terence
source.basis: The wording is nearly identical to Terence's well-known line 'amantium irae amoris integratio est' in the Andria, and it became proverbial in this form.

translations.literal: The angers of lovers [are] a renewal of love.
translations.note: Burton gives it as 'the old saying'. It is the proverbial form of a line in Terence, Andria (Act 3, Scene 3), where the text reads 'amantium irae amoris integratio est' ('integratiost'). The later proverb, which Burton quotes here, has 'redintegratio'. The sense is the same.
